name: What every community board asked the City for
blurb: This tool combines every community board's Capital and Expense Budget Requests since 2019, and the agency response to each, from NYC Open Data and the Register PDFs. Click a district on the map, compare its requests against its 311 complaints and draft the follow-up email to the agency.

name: Where Medicaid hurts, in New Yorkers' own words
blurb: Hearts & Minds gives the NYS Office of Customer Experience a radar that lays out the biggest problems people hit with Medicaid in the order they move through the program. Each problem is sized by the people affected, shaded by online mentions and paired with public YouTube stories, and the demo uses sample data.

name: Community board updates for every feed
blurb: BoardCast turns a community board's minutes, agendas or meeting transcripts into reviewed posts for X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and LinkedIn plus an email, with translations, and gives residents a citywide meeting calendar and meeting alerts.

name: Where to put a city grocery store
blurb: The tool identifies disadvantaged census tracts with high food insecurity and strong transit connectivity, then scores vacant city-owned lots as candidate store sites. Adjust the scoring weights and the top sites re-rank live.

name: Answer a City summons
blurb: This plain-language guide helps business owners who received a City summons: pick the issuing agency, enter the dates on the ticket, and see your deadlines and all four response options explained.

name: Get affordable housing approved
blurb: Pick one of three real Brooklyn affordable-housing projects, set the financing and site facts, and get a phased roadmap of every approval between you and lease-up, including the ones the subsidy itself triggers.

name: Flood risk against flood spending
blurb: This interactive dashboard connects where New York floods to where the city spends its flood-resilience capital dollars, down to the community-district level. It also plays back the May 20 flash flood across the subway and bus network over time.
builders: David A. Lee, Dean Berkowitz & Lyndsey Kaplan

name: A game that teaches 311
blurb: This video game teaches New Yorkers how to navigate 311, the city's main service request line.

name: Procurement record search
blurb: This tool lets anyone search and review city procurement records, so people who follow where public money goes can read the contracting data.

name: Live transit data for AI tools
blurb: This Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI tools check live transit reliability data, and it has passed 1,000 downloads since the event.

name: Index of NYC's public datasets
blurb: This website indexes NYC's civic data so residents and builders have one place to find the datasets the city publishes.

name: Map of NYC business health
blurb: This map shows the health of NYC businesses and where the local economy is thriving or under stress across the city.

name: Find open city bids
blurb: Vendors use this tool to find and track open NYC government bids and procurement opportunities and see where they can compete for city work.

name: Fill benefits forms by voice
blurb: This voice assistant lets New Yorkers fill out their benefits forms by talking through them instead of navigating the application on their own.
